claims.title: Rise of the Sao culture
claims.summary: South of Lake Chad the Sao began building walled towns and producing distinctive terracotta and bronze artwork, forming one of the earliest known complex societies in the region.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Cameroon: From the Sao of Lake Chad and the Bantu cradle of the Grassfields to a German colony, a divided trusteeship, and a bilingual republic still seeking its unity.", terralore.co/country/CMR/chronicle#ev-600bce-rise-of-the-sao-culture, claim TL:CMR:event:600bce:rise-of-the-sao-culture, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Bantu expansion begins
claims.summary: The Grassfields of the Cameroon-Nigeria borderlands are widely held to lie near the homeland of the Bantu languages, whose speakers spread from this region across central and southern Africa.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Cameroon: From the Sao of Lake Chad and the Bantu cradle of the Grassfields to a German colony, a divided trusteeship, and a bilingual republic still seeking its unity.", terralore.co/country/CMR/chronicle#ev-1000bce-the-bantu-expansion-begins, claim TL:CMR:event:1000bce:the-bantu-expansion-begins, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Height of the Sao city-states
claims.summary: The Sao settlements of the Lake Chad basin reached their apex between roughly the ninth and fifteenth centuries before being absorbed by neighbouring states and peoples such as the Kotoko.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Cameroon: From the Sao of Lake Chad and the Bantu cradle of the Grassfields to a German colony, a divided trusteeship, and a bilingual republic still seeking its unity.", terralore.co/country/CMR/chronicle#ev-1100-height-of-the-sao-city-states, claim TL:CMR:event:1100:height-of-the-sao-city-states, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Portuguese name the river of prawns
claims.summary: Portuguese sailors reaching the Wouri estuary named it Rio dos Camaroes, the river of prawns, after its abundant crustaceans; the name later evolved into Kamerun, Cameroun, and Cameroon.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Cameroon: From the Sao of Lake Chad and the Bantu cradle of the Grassfields to a German colony, a divided trusteeship, and a bilingual republic still seeking its unity.", terralore.co/country/CMR/chronicle#ev-1472-portuguese-name-the-river-of-prawns, claim TL:CMR:event:1472:portuguese-name-the-river-of-prawns, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Founding of the Bamum kingdom
claims.summary: The Bamum dynasty was founded by Nshare Yen, who established Foumban as the capital of a Grassfields kingdom that grew through conquest and diplomacy.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Cameroon: From the Sao of Lake Chad and the Bantu cradle of the Grassfields to a German colony, a divided trusteeship, and a bilingual republic still seeking its unity.", terralore.co/country/CMR/chronicle#ev-1394-founding-of-the-bamum-kingdom, claim TL:CMR:event:1394:founding-of-the-bamum-kingdom, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Modibo Adama founds the Adamawa Emirate
claims.summary: Acting under Usman dan Fodio, the Fulani leader Modibo Adama launched a jihad into Fombina and established the Adamawa Emirate, spreading Islam and Fulani rule across the north as part of the Sokoto Caliphate.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Cameroon: From the Sao of Lake Chad and the Bantu cradle of the Grassfields to a German colony, a divided trusteeship, and a bilingual republic still seeking its unity.", terralore.co/country/CMR/chronicle#ev-1809-modibo-adama-founds-the-adamawa-emirate, claim TL:CMR:event:1809:modibo-adama-founds-the-adamawa-emirate, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: King Njoya devises the Bamum script
claims.summary: King Ibrahim Njoya of Bamum and his palace circle created an original writing system, the Bamum script, and the Shumom language, used to record the kingdom's history, laws, and knowledge.

sources.label: Sultan Ibrahim Njoya: A Scholar-King (Bamum Script research guide)

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Cameroon: From the Sao of Lake Chad and the Bantu cradle of the Grassfields to a German colony, a divided trusteeship, and a bilingual republic still seeking its unity.", terralore.co/country/CMR/chronicle#ev-1895-king-njoya-devises-the-bamum-script, claim TL:CMR:event:1895:king-njoya-devises-the-bamum-script, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Douala treaty and German protectorate
claims.summary: The Douala kings Bell and Akwa signed a treaty of protection with German agents; Gustav Nachtigal then proclaimed a German protectorate over Kamerun, beginning colonial rule.

sources.label: A Guide to the History of Recognition: Cameroon
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Cameroon: From the Sao of Lake Chad and the Bantu cradle of the Grassfields to a German colony, a divided trusteeship, and a bilingual republic still seeking its unity.", terralore.co/country/CMR/chronicle#ev-1884-douala-treaty-and-german-protectorate, claim TL:CMR:event:1884:douala-treaty-and-german-protectorate, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: France cedes Neukamerun
claims.summary: Under the Treaty of Fez ending the Agadir crisis, France ceded the large territory of Neukamerun to Germany, expanding the colony eastward.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Cameroon: From the Sao of Lake Chad and the Bantu cradle of the Grassfields to a German colony, a divided trusteeship, and a bilingual republic still seeking its unity.", terralore.co/country/CMR/chronicle#ev-1911-france-cedes-neukamerun, claim TL:CMR:event:1911:france-cedes-neukamerun, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Kamerun campaign
claims.summary: British, French, and Belgian forces invaded German Kamerun from August 1914; after a prolonged campaign the last German garrison surrendered in early 1916.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Cameroon: From the Sao of Lake Chad and the Bantu cradle of the Grassfields to a German colony, a divided trusteeship, and a bilingual republic still seeking its unity.", terralore.co/country/CMR/chronicle#ev-1914-the-kamerun-campaign, claim TL:CMR:event:1914:the-kamerun-campaign, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Partition into French and British mandates
claims.summary: The League of Nations divided the former German colony between France, which took the larger French Cameroun, and Britain, which administered the Northern and Southern Cameroons alongside Nigeria.

sources.label: A Guide to the History of Recognition: Cameroon
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Cameroon: From the Sao of Lake Chad and the Bantu cradle of the Grassfields to a German colony, a divided trusteeship, and a bilingual republic still seeking its unity.", terralore.co/country/CMR/chronicle#ev-1919-partition-into-french-and-british-mandates, claim TL:CMR:event:1919:partition-into-french-and-british-mandates, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Founding of the UPC
claims.summary: Ruben Um Nyobe and others founded the Union des Populations du Cameroun, a nationalist party demanding immediate independence and the reunification of French and British Cameroon.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Cameroon: From the Sao of Lake Chad and the Bantu cradle of the Grassfields to a German colony, a divided trusteeship, and a bilingual republic still seeking its unity.", terralore.co/country/CMR/chronicle#ev-1948-founding-of-the-upc, claim TL:CMR:event:1948:founding-of-the-upc, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The UPC is banned
claims.summary: After waves of unrest, the French administration outlawed the UPC, pushing the movement underground and into an armed insurgency.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Cameroon: From the Sao of Lake Chad and the Bantu cradle of the Grassfields to a German colony, a divided trusteeship, and a bilingual republic still seeking its unity.", terralore.co/country/CMR/chronicle#ev-1955-the-upc-is-banned, claim TL:CMR:event:1955:the-upc-is-banned, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Killing of Ruben Um Nyobe
claims.summary: The UPC leader Ruben Um Nyobe was tracked down and shot by a French-led military unit; repression of the insurgency continued in the Bassa and Bamileke regions with heavy loss of life.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Cameroon: From the Sao of Lake Chad and the Bantu cradle of the Grassfields to a German colony, a divided trusteeship, and a bilingual republic still seeking its unity.", terralore.co/country/CMR/chronicle#ev-1958-killing-of-ruben-um-nyobe, claim TL:CMR:event:1958:killing-of-ruben-um-nyobe, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Independence of French Cameroun
claims.summary: The UN trusteeship administered by France ended and French Cameroun became an independent republic, with Ahmadou Ahidjo as its first president.

sources.label: A Guide to the History of Recognition: Cameroon
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Cameroon: From the Sao of Lake Chad and the Bantu cradle of the Grassfields to a German colony, a divided trusteeship, and a bilingual republic still seeking its unity.", terralore.co/country/CMR/chronicle#ev-1960-independence-of-french-cameroun, claim TL:CMR:event:1960:independence-of-french-cameroun, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The British Cameroons plebiscite
claims.summary: In a UN-supervised vote the Northern Cameroons chose to join Nigeria while the Southern Cameroons chose to reunite with the Republic of Cameroon.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Cameroon: From the Sao of Lake Chad and the Bantu cradle of the Grassfields to a German colony, a divided trusteeship, and a bilingual republic still seeking its unity.", terralore.co/country/CMR/chronicle#ev-1961-the-british-cameroons-plebiscite, claim TL:CMR:event:1961:the-british-cameroons-plebiscite, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Reunification and federation
claims.summary: The Southern Cameroons joined the republic to form the Federal Republic of Cameroon, uniting francophone East Cameroon and anglophone West Cameroon following the Foumban Conference.

sources.label: A Guide to the History of Recognition: Cameroon
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Cameroon: From the Sao of Lake Chad and the Bantu cradle of the Grassfields to a German colony, a divided trusteeship, and a bilingual republic still seeking its unity.", terralore.co/country/CMR/chronicle#ev-1961-reunification-and-federation, claim TL:CMR:event:1961:reunification-and-federation, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: From federation to unitary state
claims.summary: A referendum abolished the two-state federation in favour of a centralised United Republic of Cameroon, ending West Cameroon's separate autonomy.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Cameroon: From the Sao of Lake Chad and the Bantu cradle of the Grassfields to a German colony, a divided trusteeship, and a bilingual republic still seeking its unity.", terralore.co/country/CMR/chronicle#ev-1972-from-federation-to-unitary-state, claim TL:CMR:event:1972:from-federation-to-unitary-state, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Ahidjo resigns; Biya succeeds
claims.summary: Ahmadou Ahidjo unexpectedly resigned the presidency and was succeeded by his prime minister, Paul Biya.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Cameroon: From the Sao of Lake Chad and the Bantu cradle of the Grassfields to a German colony, a divided trusteeship, and a bilingual republic still seeking its unity.", terralore.co/country/CMR/chronicle#ev-1982-ahidjo-resigns-biya-succeeds, claim TL:CMR:event:1982:ahidjo-resigns-biya-succeeds, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Failed coup against Biya
claims.summary: An attempted coup by elements loyal to former president Ahidjo was suppressed within days, after which Biya tightened his hold on power.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Cameroon: From the Sao of Lake Chad and the Bantu cradle of the Grassfields to a German colony, a divided trusteeship, and a bilingual republic still seeking its unity.", terralore.co/country/CMR/chronicle#ev-1984-failed-coup-against-biya, claim TL:CMR:event:1984:failed-coup-against-biya, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Return to multiparty politics
claims.summary: Biya legalised opposition parties in 1990 and held the first multiparty presidential election in 1992, which he won amid allegations of irregularities.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Cameroon: From the Sao of Lake Chad and the Bantu cradle of the Grassfields to a German colony, a divided trusteeship, and a bilingual republic still seeking its unity.", terralore.co/country/CMR/chronicle#ev-1992-return-to-multiparty-politics, claim TL:CMR:event:1992:return-to-multiparty-politics, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Anglophone protests begin
claims.summary: Lawyers and teachers in the North-West and South-West regions launched protests against the marginalisation of English-speaking Cameroonians; a security crackdown followed.

sources.label: Cameroon (Anglophone crisis monitoring)
sources.publisher: Global Centre for the Responsibility to Protect

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Cameroon: From the Sao of Lake Chad and the Bantu cradle of the Grassfields to a German colony, a divided trusteeship, and a bilingual republic still seeking its unity.", terralore.co/country/CMR/chronicle#ev-2016-anglophone-protests-begin, claim TL:CMR:event:2016:anglophone-protests-begin, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Escalation into armed conflict
claims.summary: The protests gave way to an armed insurgency as separatists proclaimed the independent state of Ambazonia; the conflict has since killed thousands and displaced hundreds of thousands.

sources.label: Cameroon (Anglophone crisis monitoring)
sources.publisher: Global Centre for the Responsibility to Protect

claims.title: Biya re-elected at 92
claims.summary: Paul Biya won a further presidential term, extending a tenure begun in 1982; opposition figures disputed the official results.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Cameroon: From the Sao of Lake Chad and the Bantu cradle of the Grassfields to a German colony, a divided trusteeship, and a bilingual republic still seeking its unity.", terralore.co/country/CMR/chronicle#ev-2025-biya-re-elected-at-92, claim TL:CMR:event:2025:biya-re-elected-at-92, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.
